assumptions: Every event, minute, lesson use, and decision is invented for this rehearsal.
Lina already has a reusable LLM prompt and fraction-diagram template. The baseline includes their reuse.
Both imagined methods require the same objective, answer checks, feedback checks, and quality bar.
Edu-Canvas saves no meaningful drafting time. Any later advantage comes from less formatting and result interpretation.
The imagined prototype provides the functions stated in the shared protocol. No application, LLM provider, or Jev API is called.
Researcher help is included once in Edu-Canvas setup time. Zero means assumed no help, not a missing measurement.
No actual pupils participate. Learning outcomes and purchasing authority remain unknown.

sessions.event: Lina reuses her LLM prompt for the baseline. In the imagined prototype trial, she spends extra time learning full-branch review. She corrects an unclear instruction before approval. Setup includes three minutes of assumed researcher help.
sessions.decision: The first trial takes more total work. Lina agrees to another comparison because first-use setup can explain part of the cost.

sessions.event: The imagined task uses a different fraction example. Lina corrects wording that could imply only one matching fraction. A synthetic response selects 2/3 as equivalent to 1/2. Lina examines the first response and pauses progression for an equal-parts check.
sessions.decision: Drafting is already fast in both methods. Lina continues only to test whether the review and follow-up steps become shorter.

sessions.event: Lina returns without an imagined reminder. She uses the familiar review sequence and corrects an ambiguous hint. The scenario assumes that grouped response evidence reduces her follow-up work.
sessions.decision: The constructed comparison now shows less review and follow-up work. Lina keeps the LLM baseline available and tries one further lesson.

sessions.event: A fresh equivalent-fractions lesson uses the same imagined quality bar. Lina checks every answer and feedback branch. She fixes one confusing sentence before approval. No repeated prompt cycle is assumed.
sessions.decision: Lina would use the imagined prototype for this lesson type because the later review and follow-up costs are lower. She makes no claim about other subjects.

stated_preference: Lina prefers her existing LLM workflow for quick text drafts. She conditionally prefers the imagined Edu-Canvas workflow when review and follow-up actually take less work.
week_two_reason: The scripted role returns on days 8 and 12 because later sessions assume shorter review and follow-up. This is a constructed outcome, not observed retention.
next_real_test: Observe a frequent LLM user with their best reusable prompt and materials. Compare the same lesson and full review standard. Include incorrect-feedback review, corrections, researcher help, sharing, and result interpretation. Check unprompted return separately.
